message.content: {"scores":{"c1":7,"c2":5,"c3":6},"evidence":"Word count is about 115, within range. The text joins grammatically at 'spent most of my summer'. c1: It builds on the comparison by naming the Geneva marginal notes and the RSV being conversational, and it notes the readability-vs-sweep tradeoff. Only two of the 'four' versions are named, and the development of the tradeoff stays thin. c2: 'most of my summer jumping between them' is an invented personal detail. The excerpt mentions Kevin Kelly recommending versions, but calling the Geneva edition 'newer' contradicts history: the Geneva Bible predates the KJV. Adding a 1560 translation to fix KJV readability also strains plausibility. The closing 'patched together whole' is a neat line, and 'the work paid off in ways...' leans toward uplift. The voice is mostly informal and consistent. c3: There are some concrete specifics (thee/thou, margins, RSV tone), but 'stories underneath all the accumulated solemnity' and the tidy closing aphorism substitute for reasoning. The internal logic is shaky: it says 'doesn't make the stuff any more sensible', then 'paid off'."}
